headline: NetEase: game revenue slips 1.7% and EPS misses by 12% as no new hit arrives; shares fall 11% with Ananta two months away
takeaway: Revenue fell 1.8% to RMB27.9 billion and game revenue 1.7% to RMB22.9 billion. Non-GAAP earnings of US$2.13 per ADS were about 12% below the consensus even as margins improved, and the shares dropped 11% on the day as investors looked for growth that the current portfolio is not delivering.
results: NetEase reported net revenue of RMB27.9 billion (US$4.2 billion) for the third quarter, down 1.8% from a year earlier. Games and related services, about 80% of the total, fell 1.7% to RMB22.9 billion; Youdao, the education business, fell 12.3%; NetEase Cloud Music was almost flat at RMB1.9 billion; and innovative businesses grew 7.1%.

Profitability improved despite lower sales. Gross profit rose 4.8% to RMB19.0 billion and operating expenses fell 5.4% to RMB9.6 billion. Non-GAAP net income was RMB9.2 billion, or US$2.13 per ADS (about RMB14.2), against a consensus of roughly RMB16.1 and RMB14.7 a year earlier.

Operating cash flow was RMB10.5 billion, down from RMB12.9 billion a year earlier. Net cash reached RMB175.2 billion (US$26.1 billion). The company declared a dividend of US$0.585 per ADS and has bought back US$2.3 billion of stock under a US$5 billion programme extended to January 2029.
mgmt: Chief executive William Ding said NetEase remains committed to carefully crafted content and lasting player communities, and is advancing titles across genres, platforms and markets. The company highlighted continued engagement in Fantasy Westward Journey, Identity V, Eggy Party and Sword of Justice, new content for Marvel Rivals, and Where Winds Meet passing 100 million players worldwide in August.

The most important pipeline item is Ananta, an open-world urban action game scheduled for a global launch on PC, console and mobile on January 15, 2027. NetEase also began player tests for several other titles in development. As usual, it gave no financial guidance.
view: NetEase is a superb games company in an awkward phase of its cycle. Its older franchises — Fantasy Westward Journey has been running for more than twenty years — are cash machines but no longer growing, and the newer hits of 2024 and 2025, Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, have moved past their launch peaks. The result is a quarter in which revenue drifts lower while cost discipline props up profit. That is a respectable outcome for a mature business, but the market prices NetEase on its ability to produce the next hit, and this quarter had none.

The 11% fall looks like an over-reaction to a miss whose cause is mostly timing. Consensus numbers for NetEase have run ahead of the release calendar for several quarters, and the company has deliberately pulled back from a number of Western studios to concentrate spending. With US$26 billion of net cash — about 40% of the market value — a growing dividend and an active buyback, the downside is cushioned in a way few growth stocks enjoy.

The investment case now rests heavily on Ananta. It is NetEase’s most ambitious attempt at a global open-world game, competing directly with titles from miHoYo, Tencent and Kuro Games, and its launch in January will largely decide whether 2027 is a growth year. A strong launch would turn this quarter into a buying opportunity; a weak one would leave NetEase as a cash-rich company with an ageing portfolio. Investors are effectively being offered a free option on a major release at around 13 times earnings, or about eight times once the cash is set aside.
watch: Watch Ananta’s launch on January 15 and its first-month revenue rankings, whether game revenue returns to growth in the fourth quarter, and the pace of buybacks at the lower share price.
